DIF analysis via Andersen's likelihood-ratio test

Source: R/dif_lr.R
RMdifLR.Rd

Tests whether the item parameters differ between the groups of an external variable, with Andersen's likelihood-ratio (LR) test. The model is fitted by conditional maximum likelihood (CML) in the full sample and in each group. The test answers whether there is any DIF, not which items or thresholds have it. For that, use RMdifAnchor.

Usage

RMdifLR(
  data,
  dif_var,
  model = c("auto", "PCM", "RM"),
  output = c("kable", "dataframe"),
  ...
)

Arguments

data

A data.frame or matrix of item responses (non-negative integers, 0-based). One column per item, one row per person. Person IDs and grouping variables must not be included. Pass the grouping variable separately via dif_var.

dif_var

Vector of length nrow(data) (factor, character, or numeric) defining the groups, two or more. It is coerced to a factor and unused levels are dropped. Rows where dif_var is NA, and rows with no responses, are dropped with a message.

model

One of "auto" (default), "PCM", or "RM". The fit is the same for dichotomous data, where the two models coincide, so the choice only sets the label in Model. "auto" labels the result "RM" when every item is dichotomous and "PCM" otherwise. "RM" gives an error for polytomous data.

output

"kable" (default) or "dataframe".

...

Not used. Arguments that earlier versions accepted for the per-group location table and plots (level, cutoff, conf, sort, p_value, correction, alpha, plot_type, reference) give an error that points to RMdifAnchor.

Value

A one-row data.frame, or a knitr_kable of it, with Chisq (the LR statistic), df, p, Model ("PCM" or "RM"), Items, Groups, N (respondents used), N_excluded (rows dropped for a missing dif_var or no responses), N_incomplete (respondents used who skipped some items) and one n_<group> column per group.

Details

The LR statistic is twice the difference between the sum of the group conditional log-likelihoods and the full-sample one, with df equal to the extra free parameters of the group fits (Andersen, 1973). It equals eRm::LRtest() on the same data. Each fit is a CML partial credit model from psychotools::pcmodel() (a dichotomous item is a 2-category PCM). Respondents with missing responses are kept (CML uses the items they answered).

The test does not depend on how each group's scale is centred, but any comparison of single items or thresholds between groups does. Centring each group on its own mean makes real DIF in some items appear as artificial DIF in the others (Andrich & Hagquist, 2012), so this function no longer reports per-group locations. RMdifAnchor links the groups through anchor items and tests each item, threshold or threshold spacing, with a correction for multiple testing. The simulation study behind this change is reported at https://pgmj.github.io/rasch_book/chapters/dif-anchor-tests.html.

Like other global tests, the LR test becomes significant for small amounts of DIF in large samples, and has little power in small ones. RMdifImpact estimates whether the DIF matters for group comparisons and person scores.

Response categories. Every category an item uses must be used in every group, or the group fits have different thresholds and the test is not defined. The same holds when a category is used in a group only by respondents with a zero or perfect score there, since CML leaves them out. The function then stops and names the items, categories and groups (eRm::LRtest() instead left items with an unused category out of the test without saying so). With small groups this is common for sparse categories: merge them with an adjacent one, combine groups, or leave the item out.

References

Andersen, E. B. (1973). A goodness of fit test for the Rasch model. Psychometrika, 38(1), 123-140. doi:10.1007/BF02291180

Andrich, D., & Hagquist, C. (2012). Real and artificial differential item functioning. Journal of Educational and Behavioral Statistics, 37(3), 387-416. doi:10.3102/1076998611411913

See also

RMdifAnchor for anchored tests of single items, thresholds and threshold spacing, RMdifImpact for the size of the DIF's impact, RMdifGamma and RMdifTree.

Examples

# \donttest{
if (requireNamespace("eRm", quietly = TRUE)) { # for the example data
  set.seed(1)
  data("pcmdat2", package = "eRm")
  grp <- factor(sample(c("A", "B"), nrow(pcmdat2), replace = TRUE))

  RMdifLR(pcmdat2, dif_var = grp)
  RMdifLR(pcmdat2, dif_var = grp, output = "dataframe")
}
#> RMdifLR() now reports Andersen's LR test only, without the per-group location table and plots. For DIF in single items, thresholds and threshold spacing, use RMdifAnchor().
#> This message is displayed once per session.
#>      Chisq df         p Model Items Groups   N N_excluded N_incomplete n_A n_B
#> 1 4.063775  7 0.7724031   PCM     4      2 300          0            0 146 154
# }
